question: Standard precautions must be applied to which group of patients?

options.B: Patients admitted to surgical wards only
options.C: Only individuals showing active fever symptoms

explanation: Universal application protects staff and patients from unrecognized bloodborne and fluid-borne pathogens. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h1)

question: Why do nurses use standard precautions for every patient, regardless of their diagnosis?

options.A: Diagnostic tests take too long to process
options.B: Infectious status is often unknown or asymptomatic
options.C: Patients feel insulted if tested selectively
options.D: Hospital policy requires it for billing purposes

explanation: Many carriers of dangerous pathogens show no outward clinical signs upon admission. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h1)

question: How long should you rub your hands together when using an alcohol-based hand sanitizer?
explanation: Friction must be maintained long enough across all hand surfaces to effectively neutralize transient microbes. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h2)

question: After caring for a patient with Clostridioides difficile colitis, which hand hygiene method is necessary?

options.C: Wiping hands with a dry sterile gauze

explanation: Alcohol rubs fail to destroy bacterial spores, requiring physical removal via soap, water, and friction. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h2)

question: When putting on personal protective equipment (PPE), which item should you put on last?
explanation: Gloves go on last so their outer surface remains uncontaminated while adjusting other gear. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h3)

question: When must a nurse use sterile gloves instead of clean, non-sterile gloves?

options.A: During routine bed bath and linen changes
options.B: During surgical or invasive aseptic procedures

explanation: Sterile procedures demand the elimination of all transient and resident microbes to protect susceptible body cavities. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h3)

question: If safety-engineered needles are not available, what is the safe technique for recapping a used needle?

options.B: Holding the cap upright with bare fingers

explanation: The one-handed technique prevents accidental puncture of the hand holding the needle cap. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h4)

question: Why is it unsafe to reuse a syringe for another patient even if you change the needle?

options.A: Hospital accreditation standards forbid plastic recycling
options.B: The plastic barrel will crack under repeated pressure
options.C: Dosage measurements become inaccurate after one use
options.D: Internal components remain contaminated with blood or fluid

explanation: Backflow into the syringe barrel can introduce patient pathogens into multi-dose vials or subsequent injection lines. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h4)

question: Where should you cough or sneeze if you do not have a tissue?

options.A: Bare hands for quick washing later
options.D: Into the air away from nearby people

explanation: Coughing into the elbow prevents respiratory droplets from depositing onto hands that touch environmental surfaces. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h5)

question: Which type of transmission is primarily stopped by covering your cough or sneeze?
explanation: Containing sneezes and coughs stops large respiratory droplets from traveling through the air to nearby hosts. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h5)

question: Why must you physically clean medical equipment with soap and water before applying a chemical disinfectant?

options.A: Organic soil blocks disinfectants from contacting germs
options.B: Cleaning speeds up the air-drying process
options.C: Soap adds a pleasant fragrance to clinical tools
options.D: Disinfectants cannot dissolve hard plastic surfaces

explanation: Proteins and blood residues shield microorganisms, rendering chemical agents ineffective if not washed away first. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h6)

question: What is the term for inanimate objects, like bedside tables or stethoscope tubing, that can transfer germs between patients?
explanation: Fomites include surfaces and equipment that retain pathogens and transmit them to subsequent users. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h6)

question: If a nurse accidentally gets a needlestick injury, what is the very first thing they should do?

options.A: Apply an alcohol-based skin antiseptic immediately
options.B: Wash the wound thoroughly with soap and water
options.C: Squeeze the puncture site to force blood out
options.D: Fill out the formal hospital incident report form

explanation: Immediate mechanical washing reduces viral load at the wound site before post-exposure prophylaxis assessment. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h7)

question: Why is it important for a nurse to report a blood exposure injury immediately?

options.A: Vaccination records must be updated annually
options.B: Insurance compensation is denied after twelve hours
options.C: Timely post-exposure prophylaxis reduces infection risk
options.D: Hospital management requires proof for disciplinary review

explanation: Administering prophylactic medications within hours of high-risk exposure significantly lowers seroconversion rates for HIV and Hepatitis B. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T11#GNS112_U5_T11_h7)
